t: According to the golden rules of double entry, the rule for personal accounts is:
o: Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit all assets, credit all liabilities
Debit all expenses, credit all incomes
Debit the receiver, credit the giver
e: Personal accounts follow the rule debit the receiver and credit the giver. Real accounts use debit what comes in and nominal accounts use debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.

t: Two independent errors, one overstating the debit side of an account by ₹5,000 and another overstating the credit side of a different account by ₹5,000, are known as:
e: Compensating errors cancel each other's effect on the trial balance, so the trial balance agrees even though the individual accounts are wrong.

t: An asset costing ₹5,00,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum under the written-down value method. What is the depreciation charge for the second year?
e: Year 1 depreciation = 20% of 5,00,000 = ₹1,00,000, leaving a WDV of ₹4,00,000; year 2 depreciation = 20% of 4,00,000 = ₹80,000.

topic: Life Assurance Business: Important Types of Life Assurance Policies
t: Which feature is characteristic of a deferred annuity contract?
o: There is an accumulation (deferment) phase before annuity payments begin at the vesting date
Payments begin immediately on payment of the purchase price
It can be purchased only by a single premium
It never allows commutation of any part of the corpus
e: In a deferred annuity, premiums build a corpus during the deferment period and the annuity vests later; such plans commonly allow partial commutation at vesting within prescribed limits.

t: For unit linked business, IRDAI prescribes that premium income be recognised when:
e: The recognition point for linked premium is creation of the associated units, because the premium represents the policyholder's purchase of units at the applicable NAV.

t: What is the grace period allowed for payment of premium under the monthly mode of a life policy?
e: The grace period is 15 days for monthly mode and 30 days for all other modes; the policy remains in force during the grace period.

t: In Schedule 1 (Premium) of a life insurer's financial statements, how is reinsurance premium ceded presented?
o: As an operating expense in Schedule 3
As a benefit paid in Schedule 4
As a deduction from gross premium to arrive at net premium
e: Schedule 1 shows first year, renewal and single premium, adds reinsurance accepted and deducts reinsurance ceded to arrive at the net premium carried to the Revenue Account.

t: A life insurer spends ₹8 lakh on new office furniture that will be used for several years. How should this outlay be classified?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Expenditure that creates an asset giving benefit over more than one accounting period is capital expenditure and is shown in the balance sheet, with only depreciation charged to revenue each year.

t: A life insurer collected first-year premium of ₹400 crore, renewal premium of ₹1,100 crore and single premium of ₹300 crore. What percentage of total premium is renewal premium?
e: Total premium = 400 + 1,100 + 300 = ₹1,800 crore; renewal share = 1,100 / 1,800 = 61.1%. A high renewal share indicates a mature, persistent book.

t: Under IRDAI accounting norms, a maturity claim on a life policy is recognised as a liability:
o: When the policyholder submits the discharge voucher
At the end of the financial year
e: Maturity and survival benefits are accounted when due, since the insurer knows the date in advance. Death claims are accounted on intimation and surrenders on receipt of the request.

t: Surrender of a life policy is accounted for by the insurer at which point?
o: When the request for surrender is received and intimated
When the policy was first issued
Only after the surrender value is paid
e: The surrender liability is recognised when the policyholder's surrender request is received, in line with the prescribed accounting policies for benefits paid.

t: Section 47 of the Insurance Act, 1938 permits a life insurer to pay the claim amount into court when:
o: There are conflicting claims or insufficient proof of title and the insurer cannot obtain a satisfactory discharge
The policyholder had not nominated anyone
e: Section 47 allows payment into court where the insurer is satisfied the claim is payable but cannot get a satisfactory discharge because of disputes about title, protecting it from double payment.

t: A participating endowment policy has a sum assured of ₹8,00,000. The insurer declares a simple reversionary bonus of ₹45 per ₹1,000 sum assured for the year. What bonus is added to the policy for the year?
e: Bonus = 8,00,000 / 1,000 × 45 = ₹36,000. Simple reversionary bonus is computed on the sum assured only and is paid with the sum assured on maturity or death.

t: Under the IRDAI (Expenses of Management of Insurers transacting life insurance business) Regulations, 2023, the limit on expenses of management is applied:
o: Separately to each product and branch
On an aggregate basis for the insurer as a whole, computed from segment-wise allowances
e: The 2023 regulations compute the overall allowable limit as the sum of segment-wise allowances on premium, but compliance is tested at the aggregate level of the insurer, giving flexibility within the overall cap.

t: Employees' remuneration, rent, printing and stationery, advertisement and depreciation of a life insurer are reported in:
o: Schedule 3 (Operating expenses related to insurance business)
e: Schedule 3 lists operating expenses related to insurance business line by line; commission is in Schedule 2 and provisions appear in Schedule 14.

t: Which of the following is NOT permitted for the Pension and General Annuity Fund of a life insurer under the IRDAI investment pattern?
e: The pension and general annuity fund must be wholly in government securities and approved investments; the Other Investments category permitted for the Life Fund (up to 15%) is not allowed here.

t: Debt securities (other than those backing linked business) held by a life insurer are carried in the balance sheet at:
o: Market value with changes through the Revenue Account
Lower of cost or market value
Historical cost adjusted for amortisation of premium or discount
e: Non-linked debt securities are treated as held to maturity and valued at amortised cost; any premium or discount on purchase is amortised over the remaining term.

t: For valuation of listed equity shares held in a life insurer's funds, the fair value is taken as:
o: The closing price on the primary stock exchange (with the secondary exchange used if not traded on the primary)
The average of the last twelve months' prices
The issue price of the shares
The book value per share as per the latest balance sheet
e: IRDAI requires listed equities to be valued at the last quoted closing price on the designated primary exchange (NSE), falling back on the secondary exchange when not traded.

t: Under the IRDAI investment regulations, the minimum proportion of a unit linked fund that must be held in approved investments is:
e: For unit linked funds, at least 75% must be in approved investments and not more than 25% in other investments, since unitholders bear the investment risk.

t: Which section of the Insurance Act, 1938 restricts the expenses of management that a life insurer may incur?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 40B deals with limitation of expenses of management in life insurance business, with the actual limits laid down by IRDAI regulations. Section 40C covers general insurance, Section 41 prohibits rebates and Section 45 relates to repudiation of policies.

t: A life insurer's Life Fund is ₹5,000 crore of which ₹1,000 crore is in Central Government securities. What further amount must be invested in Central Government securities to comply with the minimum requirement?
e: The minimum is 25% of ₹5,000 crore = ₹1,250 crore. Existing holding is ₹1,000 crore (20%), so a further ₹250 crore is needed.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Which form prescribes the Profit and Loss Account (Shareholders' Account) of a life insurer?
e: Form A-PL is the shareholders' (non-technical) account for life insurers; Form B series applies to general insurers.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: In the balance sheet of a life insurer, investments pertaining to policyholders' funds are shown in:
e: Schedule 8 is shareholders' investments, Schedule 8A is policyholders' investments and Schedule 8B is assets held to cover linked liabilities. Schedule 9 covers loans.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Assets held to cover linked liabilities are matched in the balance sheet by:
o: Provision for linked liabilities shown under policyholders' funds
e: The unit fund assets in Schedule 8B are backed by the provision for linked liabilities within policyholders' funds; both are carried at fair value so that unit values are reflected consistently.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: The surplus of the Policyholders' Account that is allocated to shareholders reaches the Profit and Loss Account through:
o: A transfer shown as amounts transferred from the Policyholders' Account (Technical Account)
Adjusting the Fair Value Change Account
e: Form A-PL starts with amounts transferred from the Policyholders' Account, to which the shareholders' own investment income and expenses are added before arriving at profit before tax.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: A life insurer's balance sheet shows shareholders' funds of ₹2,000 crore, policyholders' funds of ₹48,000 crore and funds for future appropriations of ₹500 crore, with no borrowings. What is the total of the Application of Funds side?
e: Sources of funds = 2,000 + 48,000 + 500 = ₹50,500 crore, and by the dual aspect principle the application of funds (investments, loans, fixed assets, net current assets) must equal the same total.

t: The Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021 raised the permissible foreign direct investment limit in Indian insurance companies to:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2021 amendment raised the FDI cap from 49% (set by the 2015 amendment) to 74% under the automatic route, subject to safeguards on board composition and retention of profits.

t: A budget manual in an organisation serves primarily to:
o: Record the actual expenses of the finance department
Set out the responsibilities, procedures, formats and timetable for preparing and operating budgets
List the investment limits set by IRDAI
e: The budget manual documents who does what and when in the budgeting process, ensuring consistency and coordination across departments.

t: In budgeting, the key factor (or limiting factor) refers to:
o: The factor whose influence restricts the level of activity and must therefore be considered first
The largest item of fixed cost
The department with the highest budget
The chairman's approval of the budget
e: The limiting factor (for example, trained agency force or capital available) constrains output, so the budget for that factor is prepared first and other functional budgets are built around it.

t: A policy servicing unit has fixed costs of ₹50 lakh per year and variable costs of ₹200 per policy serviced. What is the flexible budget cost for servicing 40,000 policies?
e: Flexible budget = Fixed cost + (Variable cost per unit × Activity) = 50,00,000 + 200 × 40,000 = 50,00,000 + 80,00,000 = ₹1.30 crore.

t: In the IFRS 17 / Ind AS 117 measurement model, the risk adjustment for non-financial risk represents:
o: The compensation the insurer requires for bearing uncertainty about the amount and timing of cash flows from insurance risk
The discount rate used to value cash flows
The unearned profit on the contract
e: The risk adjustment is an explicit margin added to the present value of fulfilment cash flows for uncertainty from non-financial (insurance, lapse, expense) risk; the unearned profit is the contractual service margin.

t: The value of new business (VNB) margin disclosed by listed Indian life insurers is computed as:
o: VNB divided by annualised premium equivalent (APE)
e: VNB margin = value of new business / APE, showing the profitability of each rupee of annualised new business premium written in the period.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: A life insurer's liability for gratuity and other long-term employee benefits must be measured on an actuarial basis under:
o: AS 11 - Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
e: AS 15 requires defined benefit obligations such as gratuity and leave encashment to be measured using the projected unit credit method with actuarial valuation.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: Which Accounting Standard governs the recognition of provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets, relevant to disclosure of pending litigation against an insurer?
e: AS 29 requires a provision when there is a present obligation with a probable outflow that can be reliably estimated; otherwise the item is disclosed as a contingent liability, as insurers do for policy-related claims in dispute.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: Which statement about the application of Accounting Standards to Indian life insurers is correct?
o: Accounting Standards do not apply to insurers at all
Accounting Standards issued by ICAI apply to the extent they are not inconsistent with the IRDAI regulations and the Insurance Act
Insurers may choose any national or international standards
Only Ind AS applies to insurers since 2016
e: Insurers follow the ICAI Accounting Standards, but where the IRDAI financial statement regulations prescribe a different treatment (for example on investments or premium recognition) the regulations prevail.

t: The claims settlement ratio of a life insurer is generally computed as:
o: Claims paid divided by premium income
Number of claims settled divided by the total number of claims intimated (including those outstanding at the start) in the period
Claims outstanding divided by life fund
Claims paid divided by sum assured in force
e: The settlement ratio shows the proportion of claims received that were settled during the period and is widely used by consumers to judge an insurer's claims performance.

t: A life insurer issued 10,000 policies in a year. At the end of thirteen months from issue, 8,500 of these policies are still in force. What is its 13th month persistency (by count)?
e: Persistency = policies in force / policies issued = 8,500 / 10,000 = 85%. The remaining 15% represents lapses or surrenders in the first year.

t: A life insurer earned profit after tax of ₹600 crore on an average net worth of ₹4,000 crore. Its return on equity is:
e: Return on equity = Profit after tax / Net worth = 600 / 4,000 = 15%, indicating the return generated for shareholders on their capital.

t: The commission ratio of a life insurer is defined as:
o: Commission paid as a percentage of premium
Commission paid as a percentage of total expenses
Commission paid as a percentage of net worth
Commission paid as a percentage of claims
e: Commission ratio = commission / premium (gross written premium), and is monitored alongside the operating expense ratio to assess distribution cost efficiency.

t: The committee whose 1994 report recommended opening up the Indian insurance sector to private and foreign participation was headed by:
e: The Malhotra Committee (1994) recommended private entry, an independent regulator and foreign participation, leading eventually to the IRDA Act, 1999.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act was enacted in the year:
e: The IRDA Act, 1999 established the regulator, which was constituted in April 2000; the 2015 amendment later renamed it as IRDAI and raised FDI to 49%.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: Under the net present value (NPV) criterion, a capital project should be accepted when:
o: Its payback period is less than two years
Its NPV at the company's cost of capital is positive
Its accounting rate of return exceeds the inflation rate
Its total undiscounted cash inflows exceed the outlay
e: A positive NPV means the discounted cash inflows exceed the investment at the required rate of return, adding value to the firm; payback and undiscounted totals ignore the time value of money.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: A life insurer invests ₹60 lakh in a new policy administration system that is expected to save ₹15 lakh every year. What is the payback period?
e: Payback period = Initial outlay / Annual cash inflow = 60 / 15 = 4 years. Payback ignores cash flows after recovery and the time value of money.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: Which statement about the duration of a bond portfolio is correct?
o: A portfolio with longer duration is more sensitive to changes in interest rates
Duration is unaffected by the coupon rate
A zero coupon bond has a duration shorter than its maturity
e: Duration measures price sensitivity to interest rate changes; the longer the duration the greater the sensitivity, which is why ALM compares asset and liability durations.

t: For a life policy issued on or after 1 April 2012, the maturity proceeds are exempt under Section 10(10D) only if the annual premium does not exceed what percentage of the actual capital sum assured?
e: Policies issued on or after 1 April 2012 must have premium within 10% of sum assured (15% for persons with disability or specified disease, for policies issued on or after 1 April 2013) to qualify for exemption.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: Which statement about Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) under Section 115JB and life insurance companies is correct?
o: MAT applies to life insurers at 15% of book profit
MAT does not apply to income from life insurance business
MAT applies only to foreign life insurers
MAT replaces the 12.5% rate under Section 115B
e: Section 115JB(5A) provides that MAT provisions do not apply to income accruing from life insurance business, which is taxed under Section 115B at 12.5%.

topic: Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Act
t: Under the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, records of transactions must be maintained by an insurer for a period of:
o: 5 years from the date of transaction
e: Transaction records are to be kept for five years from the date of the transaction, and identity records for five years after the business relationship ends.

topic: Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Act
t: Who is responsible within a life insurance company for furnishing reports such as CTR and STR to the Financial Intelligence Unit - India?
o: The Principal Officer designated under the AML guidelines
e: The AML/CFT guidelines require each insurer to designate a Principal Officer responsible for compliance and reporting to FIU-IND, along with a Designated Director.
